title: The Quran Has a Tell for Whether It Will Answer Its Own Question
excerpt: The Quran keeps asking 'and what will make you know what this is?' — and a single letter tells you if an answer is coming. With the perfect-tense verb adrāka (13 times), the very next line always answers (al-Ḥuṭamah, Laylat al-Qadr, al-Qariah). With the imperfect-tense yudrīka (exactly 3 times), the answer never comes — only 'perhaps': the Hour's timing (33:63, 42:17) and a soul's future (80:3). The tense sorts what the Quran opens from what it keeps sealed.
seo_title: Wa-mā adrāka vs wa-mā yudrīka: How One Verb Tense Signals a Quranic Answer
seo_description: A corpus-verified reading: the Quran's rhetorical question uses adrāka (perfect, 13×) when an answer follows in the next line, and yudrīka (imperfect, 3×) when the answer is withheld — the Hour and a soul's end. The verb aspect marks knowable from sealed.
